title: Trump plans to grow his way out of $40 trillion debt crisis—it’s a ‘fantastic story’ but virtually impossible, says top budget economist
summary:
The U.S. national debt has hit $40 trillion, and the Trump administration is facing questions about its budget plans as a result.
The good news is, there has one: The American economy will apparently grow its way out of any fiscal crisis.
And the way you take care of debt is with growth, and we have tremendous growth.
When the alternative is cutting borrowing and, as a result, government spending, the growth plan is a more optimistic and politically palatable route.
Trump later suggested a "golden visa" strategy—selling rich immigrants visas at $5 million each—could pay down the national debt.

title: The $40 trillion national debt and the bond market’s revolt: top Wall Street strategists explain how we got into this mess
summary:
They also got a major helping hand from an AI-assisted column in the Wall Street Journal by hedge fund legend Stanley Druckenmiller.
The math behind the milestoneKelly's note draws a distinction that matters more than the $40 trillion headline number itself.
That figure is total federal public debt outstanding, which includes roughly $7.8 trillion the government owes its own trust funds.
The measure economists actually watch—debt held by the public—will end this fiscal year at $32.3 trillion, or 100.5% of GDP, J.P. Morgan projects.
That ratio was just 34.7% as recently as fiscal 2000, when the federal government posted a $236 billion surplus.

title: Sam Altman says the economy is adapting to AI slower than he expected
summary:
Sam Altman says he misjudged how quickly AI would scramble the economy.
"I think it means we've all been too ambitious on timelines," Altman said.
AI labs — including OpenAI and Anthropic — have spent years promoting the technology's potential to make companies leaner, start new businesses with fewer employees, and transform the economy.
Anthropic's CEO Dario Amodei famously said the tech could eliminate 50% of all entry-level white-collar work in five years.
Silicon Valley's AI predictions have had sweeping impacts, with consequences reverberating all the way to Wall Street.

title: Dollar Debasement Frees Emerging-Markets Currencies From Treasuries’ Weight
summary:
(Bloomberg) -- US Treasuries and emerging-market currencies are diverging the most in more than four years as higher US yields fail to fuel the dollar's strength like they once did.
MSCI Inc.'s benchmark for emerging-market currencies, meanwhile, is on track for its biggest quarterly gain in more than a year.
Developing nations have attracted global flows this year as investors seek higher yields and diversify portfolios away from dollar-denominated assets.
A cheaper dollar makes commodities less expensive for countries with other currencies and thus boost their demand.

title: Trump says the US doesn’t need Canada. The economy says otherwise
summary:
TORONTO (AP) — U.S. President Donald Trump says his country does not need Canada.
But every day, roughly 4 million barrels of Canadian crude oil flow south, helping fuel American cars, trucks and airplanes and supply U.S. industry.
"WE DON'T NEED CANADA, THEY NEED US!"
Daniel Béland, a political science professor at McGill University, said Trump's claim that the U.S. doesn't need Canada is "absolutely false," citing U.S. reliance on Canadian oil and natural gas and deeply integrated industries such as autos.
Much of that gap reflects U.S. purchases of Canadian energy, which helps power the U.S. economy.

title: What Growing Businesses Should Expect From an HR and Payroll Provider
summary:
Providers are increasingly introducing managed payroll services, HR advisory offerings and support models that supplement teams rather than replace them.
As a result, business leaders are asking different questions when evaluating HR and payroll providers.

title: ‘This is crazy. This is insane’: Bill Gates has changed his mind about AI and jobs
summary:

title: Andy Burnham calls National Economic Council summit with UK nations
summary:
Andy Burnham says he will bring together the leaders of Wales, Scotland and Northern Ireland this autumn for a summit to help boost the UK economy.
The first ministers of Wales and Scotland, and the first and deputy first ministers of Northern Ireland will meet Burnham at the National Economic Council in October.
The National Economic Council was created by Gordon Brown's UK government in the wake of the 2008 banking crash, and has now been revived by Burnham.
Plaid Cymru Deputy First Minister of Wales Sioned Williams, speaking before she met Burnham at the visit to the steelworks, said she thought "the announcement about the National Economic Council is a hopeful thing".
"We can discuss challenges there, we can discuss how every postcode, as the prime minister has put it, needs to see economic growth.

title: Papa Johns Sales Are Down in the U.S. — But It Just Found a New Growth Partner on the Other Side of the Border
summary:
Listen to this postPapa Johns is looking south of the border for a fresh slice of growth.
The chain named KM Capital, a Mexico-based investment firm founded in 1986, as its new franchise partner there.
KM Capital is taking over 44 existing Papa Johns restaurants and plans to keep investing in operations, branding and growth across the country, according to NRN.
“Mexicans have a strong passion for pizza, and we see an opportunity to grow the Papa Johns’ brand,” said Enrique Ruiz Mandujano, the firm’s CEO.
Papa Johns’ international business just posted its seventh straight quarter of positive same-store sales, up 1.5% in Q2.
